code: #' @param lm_method character. Linear model method for interaction testing. #'   Default: "gam" (generalized additive model). #'   Choices: "lmm" (linear mixed model), "gam", "fpca" (functional PCA), "gee" (generalized estimating equations). #'    #'   **Important:** Different methods produce different p-values and effect sizes. #'   Reproducible analyses must document which method was used. #' #' @param lm_pcorr character. P-value correction method for LM interaction tests. #'   Default: "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg, controls FDR). #'   Choices: "BH", "bonferroni" (controls FWER, most conservative),  #'            "hochberg", "holm". #'    #'   **Important:** Different methods have different stringency. Must match #'   between analyses for reproducibility. #' #' @param divergence_ci numeric. Confidence interval level for divergence calculations. #'   Default: 0.95 (95% CI). #'   Range: 0 to 1. #'    #'   **Important:** Currently hardcoded to 0.95 in core function; this parameter #'   allows override without modifying code. #' #' @param divergence_control_group character or NULL. Reference group for pairwise #'   divergence comparisons. Default: NULL (compares all groups). #'    #'   **Important:** Specifying a control group ensures all comparisons are #'   relative to a baseline. #' #' @param jis_use_lm_fdr logical. Whether to use FDR-corrected (TRUE) or raw #'   p-values (FALSE) from LM results when filtering in isoform switching analysis. #'   Default: TRUE (use FDR-corrected). #'    #'   **Important:** Different choices dramatically affect number of genes selected #'   for switching detection. Must match between analyses.

code: **Bootstrap Method Recommendation for Bounded Data:**  When analyzing Tsallis entropy (or other bounded distributions like proportions or probabilities): \itemize{   \item \strong{Use} \code{bootstrap_method = "bca"} (bias-corrected and accelerated)   \item \strong{NOT} \code{bootstrap_method = "percentile"}   \item \strong{Reason:} Percentile bootstrap assumes symmetric distribution;     entropy is inherently bounded (0 to log N) and skewed. BCA adjusts for this skewness     and produces valid confidence intervals that contain the point estimate.   \item \strong{Citation:} References C016 (2005), C030 (2023), S115 (2015) }  **Method Selection Impact:**  The choice of \code{lm_method} significantly affects results: \itemize{   \item \code{lm_method = "gam"}: Smooth fit over q-spectrum; good for curved relationships   \item \code{lm_method = "lmm"}: Mixed effects; better for complex hierarchical structure   \item \code{lm_method = "fpca"}: Functional principal component analysis; good for functional data   \item \code{lm_method = "gee"}: Generalized estimating equations; good for correlated observations }  Different methods may produce different p-values and effect sizes. Document your choice in analysis reports and use the same method across comparable analyses.

text: Default value: "percentile" Type: character controls: Bootstrap confidence interval construction algorithm "percentile": Simple percentile bootstrap, assumes symmetric distribution "bca": Bias-corrected accelerated bootstrap, adjusts skewness bias Distribution shape matters: Tsallis entropy naturally bounded [0, log(m)], often skewed Percentile CI may contain point estimate distribution skewed (invalid coverage) BCA corrects costs ~20-50% computation percentile: Fast potentially invalid CIs skewed data (common entropy) bca: valid CIs especially bounded distributions (RECOMMENDED Tsallis entropy) Citation: Papers C016 (2005), C030 (2023), S115 (2015) show bounded Tsallis entropy exhibits skewness requiring BCA Decision rule: Use "bca" entropy analysis; use "percentile" ’ve verified symmetry

text: Current location: documented calculate_diversity_s4() @param section Default value: FALSE Type: logical controls: Whether compute bootstrap confidence intervals around entropy/divergence estimates Statistical importance: WITHOUT bootstrap: point estimates (uncertainty quantification). bootstrap: point + CI bounds FALSE: Fast (1x computation), output diversity/divergence assay, ci_lower/ci_upper assays TRUE: Slower (5-10x depending nboot), adds ci_lower/ci_upper assays bounds Via function: calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, bootstrap=TRUE, nboot=1000) Via config: seq_config <- tsenat_config(); seq_config$bootstrap <- TRUE PROBLEM: tsenat_config() signature, can’t pass directly config creation use: Always TRUE publication results; FALSE exploratory/quick checks Recommendation: ADD tsenat_config() default=FALSE backward compatibility

title: TSENAT Statistical Parameters Audit
text: Current location: documented calculate_diversity_s4() .calculate_diversity() help Default value: 0 NULL (interpreted pseudocount) Type: numeric character (“auto”) controls: Pseudocount added transcript counts entropy calculation zero counts: log(0) = -∞ causing NaN/Inf entropy values Pseudocount prevents zero-division: (count + pseudocount) / (total + pseudo*n_transcripts) Acts regularization: lower values = variance, higher values = bias 0 NULL: pseudocount (raw entropy, risky sparse genes zero-count samples) 0.5: Half-count pseudocount (edgeR default, standard practice) 1.0: Full pseudocount (DESeq2 default, conservative) "auto": Automatically estimated based library size via .estimate_pseudocount() (RECOMMENDED) 0: Entropy values genes zero-count sample NaN 0.5-1.0: Prevents NaN, adds small bias, reduces variance (Bayesian regularization) "auto": Adapts pseudocount sequencing depth (principled approach, used edgeR/DESeq2) Via function: calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, pseudocount=0.5) Via config: need expose tsenat_config() Citation: Robinson et al. 2010 (edgeR paper S001), Li et al. 2023 (bootstrapped entropy validation) CRITICAL: Document “auto” RECOMMENDED real data

text: Current location: documented calculate_diversity_s4() @param section Default value: 0.95 Type: numeric (0 < bootstrap_ci < 1) controls: Confidence interval level (0.90 = 90% CI, 0.95 = 95% CI, 0.99 = 99% CI) Statistical importance: Users may require different CI levels depending publication standards risk tolerance 0.90: Narrower CI (faster computation), used resources limited preliminary results 0.95: Standard/default (widest common CI), best balance publication 0.99: Conservative, wide CI, used false positive risk must minimized Via function: calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, bootstrap_ci=0.99) need tsenat_config() field Recommendation: ADD tsenat_config() default=0.95

title: TSENAT Statistical Parameters Audit
text: Current location: documented calculate_diversity_s4() .calculate_diversity() help Default value: "none" Type: character Options: "none", "empirical_bayes" controls: Entropy estimation variance reduction via Bayesian shrinkage toward global mean Gene 1 isoform: entropy = 0 (deterministic), high variance estimate Shrinkage: borrows information genes, reduces estimate variance "none": Raw entropy per gene, information borrowing (higher variance sparse genes) "empirical_bayes": Shrunk estimates toward global mean (lower variance, reduced false positives noise) Use "none" small datasets (<50 genes) global mean unreliable Use "empirical_bayes" moderate/large datasets (>100 genes) borrowing strength valid Mathematical basis: Papers S004-S006 validate empirical Bayes strengthening entropy estimation Accessibility: Via function: calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, shrinkage="empirical_bayes") Recommendation: ADD tsenat_config() default=“none”

title: TSENAT Statistical Parameters Audit
text: Current location: PARTIALLY documented calculate_diversity_s4() help , tsenat_config() Default value: NULL (post-hoc normalization) Type: character NULL NULL: post-hoc normalization (initial norm applied) "default": Simple range normalization [0,1] theoretical maximum "zscore": Z-score normalization per q-value: (diversity - mean) / sd "log_odds_ratio": Log-odds ratio relative max entropy "relative_reference": Divide reference group mean (requires reference_group param) controls: POST-HOC normalization applied primary diversity calculation normalization: Entropy scale depends isoform count, comparable across genes Range [0,1]: Standardizes within gene, comparable within-gene across q-values Z-score: Enables cross-q comparison, removes q-specific scale effects Log-odds-ratio: Interpretation relative random expectation (isoform-aware) Relative-reference: Normalization reference group (control group) comparative analysis Impact results: Dramatically changes scale interpretability Accessibility: Via function: calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, norm_method="zscore") Recommendation: ADD tsenat_config() clear documentation appropriate Citation: Papers B002-B007 validate different normalization methods; I023 (Hill numbers) discusses standardization

what: Section 7: Proposed Revised “Statistical Inference Methods” Section
title: Comprehensive Evaluation: README Statistical Inference Methods Section
code: ## Statistical Inference Methods  TSENAT implements a comprehensive, method-flexible statistical framework optimized  for entropy-based isoform diversity analysis:  ### Linear Modeling Approaches (Choose one)  - **Generalized Additive Models (GAM/GAMM)** [DEFAULT]: Flexible smoothing with    adaptive basis functions. For paired designs, uses GAMM with AR(1) autocorrelation.    Automatically selects family (Beta for bounded [0,1], Gamma for heteroscedastic,    Gaussian otherwise).  - **Linear Mixed Models (LMM)**: Parametric framework with AR(1) correlation structure    for repeated measures. Use when residuals are approximately normal and parametric    inference is preferred.  - **Functional Principal Component Analysis (FPCA)**: Treats entropy curves across    q-values as functional objects; extracts orthogonal functional components and    performs ANOVA. Ideal for multi-scale (q-spectrum) comparative analysis.  - **Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE)**: Semi-parametric approach using working    correlation structures. Robust alternative to mixed models for non-normal, correlated    outcomes.  ### Rank-Based and Distribution-Free Tests  - **Friedman Rank Test** [DEFAULT for paired]: Maximal robustness for paired designs;    ideal for bounded, non-normal distributions like entropy.  - **Kendall Test**: Alternative rank-based approach with different power characteristics.  - **Wilcoxon Paired Test**: For pairwise comparisons within groups.  - **Conditional Rank Tests**: Stratified rank testing within strata.  ### Permutation and Resampling Methods  - **Permutation Testing**: Distribution-free testing via sample permutation.  - **Westfall-Young Permutation (WY) Correction**: Advanced permutation-based    multiple testing correction controlling family-wise error rate (FWER) with    stepdown procedure; more powerful than traditional Bonferroni.  - **Pairwise Permutation Testing**: Shuffling-based testing for pairwise comparisons.  ### Bootstrap Confidence Intervals  - **Percentile Bootstrap** [DEFAULT]: Computes percentile CI from resampled bootstrap    distribution. Fast but assumes symmetric distribution.  - **Bias-Corrected and Accelerated (BCA) Bootstrap** [RECOMMENDED for entropy]: Adjusts    for skewness and bias; ideal for bounded, skewed entropy distributions. Includes    diagnostics (skewness, acceleration factor).  ### Effect Size and Outlier Assessment  - **M-Estimation** (Huber, Tukey weights): Dual role—computes outlier-resistant effect    sizes for divergence analysis AND provides influence-based QC analysis identifying    samples with disproportionate effect on results.  ### Isoform-Level Switching Analysis  - **Jackknife Resampling**: Bootstrap-based leave-one-transcript-out approach identifying    which transcripts drive observed diversity shifts. Delta influence weighting measures    each transcript's contribution across replicates. Support frequency thresholding (e.g.,    90% of bootstrap samples) identifies robust switching signals. Also includes entropy    outlier detection via traditional leave-one-out jackknife.  ### Multiple Testing Corrections  - **Benjamini-Hochberg (BH)** [DEFAULT]: Controls False Discovery Rate (FDR).  - **Bonferroni**: Conservative family-wise error rate (FWER) control.  - **Holm Step-Down**: Less conservative than Bonferroni, controls FWER.  - **Westfall-Young Permutation**: Permutation-based FWER control with stepdown.  ---  **Guidance**: Default configuration (`tsenat_config()`) uses GAM + BH + Friedman (paired)  + BCA bootstrap, tuned for entropy analysis. Adjust via `lm_method`, `lm_pcorr`,  `bootstrap_method` parameters to match your study design and assumptions.

title: Tsallis Entropy: Comprehensive Mathematical Enhancements for TSENAT Documentation
code: ## The Mathematics Behind Tsallis Entropy  ### Core Formula and Generalization  Tsallis entropy is defined as:  $$S_q = \frac{1 - \sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i^q}{q - 1}$$  where $p_i$ represents the proportion of each isoform $i$ within a gene (with $\sum p_i = 1$),  $n$ is the number of expressed isoforms, and $q \geq 0$ is the diversity order parameter.  This elegant formula generalizes Shannon entropy (recovered when $q \to 1$) and enables  tuning sensitivity to different facets of isoform organization. By sliding $q$ across scales,  you zoom from rare isoform variants (small $q$) to dominant transcript patterns (large $q$),  capturing biological signal invisible to fixed-scale methods.  ### Special Cases and Interpretation  The $q$ parameter functions as a **sensitivity dial** for different scales of isoform complexity:  - **q = 0 (Richness)**: $S_0 = \log n$ — Simple count of expressed isoforms. Emphasizes    rare variants most strongly; only asks "how many distinct isoforms exist?" regardless of abundance.    - **q = 1 (Shannon Entropy)**: $S_1 = -\sum p_i \ln p_i$ — Standard information-theoretic measure.    Balanced weighting across all abundance scales. This is the foundational reference point where    uncertainty and information content are optimally defined.    - **q = 2 (Gini-Simpson Index)**: $S_2 = 1 - \sum p_i^2$ — Probability that two randomly-drawn    transcripts are different types. Naturally bounded in [0, 1]; **de-emphasizes rare variants**    quadratically, making it robust to sampling noise and low-abundance isoforms.  ### Bounded Range and Normalization  Tsallis entropy is mathematically **bounded** for each gene:  $$0 \leq S_q \leq S_{q,\max} = \frac{1 - n^{1-q}}{q - 1}$$  where the maximum is achieved when all $n$ isoforms are equally abundant. TSENAT computes  **normalized entropy** by division: $\tilde{S}_q = S_q / S_{q,\max}$, producing values in [0, 1]  that are directly comparable across genes with different isoform counts. This normalization enables  detection of diversity shifts independent of whether genes reorganize rare variants or major isoforms.  ### Information-Theoretic Weighting: Why q Matters  The parameter $q$ quantifies how much **weight each isoform receives**:  - **Low q (< 1)**: Enhances (emphasizes) rare isoforms. A minority transcript contributes    proportionally more to the entropy sum. Reveals "hidden complexity" in genes where one isoform    dominates but others provide substrate for regulatory flexibility.    - **Mid q (≈ 1)**: Balanced, foundational weighting. All isoforms contribute proportionally to their    abundance. This is the maximally-informative scale for general diversity assessment.    - **High q (> 2)**: Depresses (downweights) rare isoforms. Only abundant transcripts substantially    affect entropy. Captures "robust" isoforms that persist across perturbations and evolutionary time.  This flexibility is formalized in generalized entropy frameworks (Tsallis, Rényi, Hill numbers) and  reflects the principle that organismal systems often require **multi-scale surveillance**: detecting  both rare innovations (low-q window) and robust functions (high-q window).  ### The q-Curve: Detecting Scale-Dependent Isoform Switching  By computing $S_q$ across a range of q-values (typically 0 to 2 in TSENAT), you obtain a complete  **diversity profile** or "q-curve" for each gene. This curve reveals the **organizational structure**  of isoform abundance:  - **Flat q-curve**: Isoform diversity is consistent across scales. Suggests balanced repertoire;    reorganization between conditions affects all isoforms proportionally.    - **Steep slope in q-curve**: Diversity drops sharply at high q. Suggests one or few dominant    isoforms with many minor variants. Reorganization would involve shifting which isoform dominates    (classic isoform switching).    - **Changing slope across conditions**: Indicates **scale-dependent isoform switching**—gene reorganizes    differently at different abundance scales. This is the hallmark of regulatory flexibility and the    primary signal TSENAT detects.  For complete mathematical treatment and biological interpretation, see `vignette("TSENAT")`.

title: Tsallis Entropy: Comprehensive Mathematical Enhancements for TSENAT Documentation
text: Add vignette “Special Cases Limiting Behavior” section:
code: **Bounded Range and Normalization**: Tsallis entropy is bounded above for each finite sample  of $n$ isoforms:  $$S_{q,\max}(n) = \frac{1 - n^{1-q}}{q - 1}$$  This maximum is achieved only when all isoforms are equally abundant ($p_i = 1/n$ for all $i$).  In TSENAT, entropy values are normalized by this maximum via division, producing standardized  scores in [0, 1] comparable across genes regardless of isoform count. This is essential for:  1. **Cross-gene comparison**: A gene with 100 isoforms cannot have the same maximum entropy     as a gene with 5 isoforms without normalization.     2. **Robust statistical testing**: Normalized scores have comparable variance structure across     genes, improving power for detecting interactions and group effects.     3. **Biological interpretability**: A normalized value of 0.8 means "80% of maximal possible     diversity for this gene," allowing intuitive understanding regardless of gene complexity.

code: **Practical Weighting Intuition**:   Consider a gene with one dominant isoform (95%) and four minor ones (1.25% each):  | q value | Contribution of rare isoform | Interpretation | |---------|-------------------------------|-----------------| | q = 0   | 100% (included in count)      | "Diversity exists" | | q = 0.5 | p^0.5 = √0.0125 ≈ 11% effect | Low weighting, but matters | | q = 1   | p^1 = 0.0125 = 1.25% effect   | Shannon baseline | | q = 2   | p^2 = 0.00016 ≈ 0.016% effect | Rare variant nearly ignored |  This shows why q-spectrum is powerful: the same gene appears **highly diverse** at low q  (rare variants are real) but **low diversity** at high q (dominated by single isoform).  A group comparison revealing **change** only at high q suggests differential usage of  the dominant isoform, while change at low q suggests rare isoform switching.

text: Biological systems operate processes fundamentally different organizational scales. single gene’s expression can viewed different “lenses”-perspective dominant isoforms (high q, emphasizing abundant variants) rare isoforms may carry functional significance specific contexts (low q, emphasizing rare variants). LM interaction test revealed condition effects vary across diversity scales (q parameter), reflecting biological reorganization can manifest differently depending aspect isoform complexity examine. theoretical foundation scale-dependent analysis comes generalized entropy measures. Renyi’s entropy family (Rényi 1961) introduced continuous spectrum diversity measures parameterized sensitivity index, Tsallis later extended popularized (Alomani Kayid 2023). Unlike Shannon entropy (represents single point spectrum), Tsallis entropy provides family measures parameter q acts “magnifying glass”-adjusting organizational scales become visible. Mathematically, different q-values weight rare versus abundant isoforms differently: Low q (0-0.5): Emphasized rare isoforms, revealing exploratory conditional splicing programs Mid q (0.5-1.5): Balanced sensitivity across full isoform distribution High q (1.5-2.0): Emphasized abundant isoforms, revealing core splicing decisions biological systems, different scales often correspond different regulatory mechanisms. transcript may consistently rare across conditions (switching low q) stably abundant high q. Detecting scale-specific switching patterns reveals mechanistic structure splicing regulation (Tarabichi et al. 2013).

what: S4 Workflow: Unified Analysis via TSENATAnalysis Objects
title: TSENAT: Tsallis Entropy Analysis Toolbox
text: TSENAT provides integrated S4-based workflow coordinated analysis following three principles: Configure : Use tsenat_config() specify analysis parameters (q-values, metadata columns) Run pipeline: Use tsenat() orchestrate analysis steps sequence Access results: Use S4 accessor methods type-safe result retrieval tsenat() function accepts configured TSENATConfig object orchestrates complete pipeline: diversity computation -> quality control -> statistical testing -> effect sizes (specified methods parameter). Parameter verbose = TRUE outputs progress messages showing data filtering steps method completion. single-function approach ensures consistency preprocessing analysis steps, eliminating boilerplate reducing risk parameter mismatches. Accessor methods return types: accessors return SummarizedExperiment objects (following Bioconductor conventions) containing results assays metadata: diversity(analysis) -> SummarizedExperiment (genes x samples, multiple assays q-value) lmResults(analysis) -> list containing data.frame LM interaction results jeoResults(analysis, q = 1.0) -> SummarizedExperiment jackknife entropy outlier confidence intervals jisResults(analysis, q = 1.0) -> list jackknife isoform switching results rankResults(analysis) -> data.frame rank test results divergence(analysis) -> SummarizedExperiment pairwise divergence metrics requested method run tsenat() orchestration, accessor returns NULL-users check results downstream use. detailed step--step implementation, see sections demonstrating analysis component accessor patterns.
code: # Configure analysis parameters once (best practice for reproducibility) tsenat_config <- tsenat_config(   q_values = seq(0, 2, by = 0.05),   sample_col = "sample",   condition_col = "condition",   subject_col = "paired_samples",   nthreads = 2 )  ## Build a complete `TSENATAnalysis` object analysis <- build_analysis_s4(   config = config,   readcounts = readcounts,   metadata = metadata_df,   tx2gene = gff3_file,    tpm = tpm,   effective_length = effective_length )  # Run complete pipeline with one function call orchestrating all specified methods # methods parameter: vector of analysis steps to execute ("diversity", "lm_interaction", "jackknife", "divergence") # verbose = TRUE: prints progress messages showing gene filtering, step completion, and result summaries analysis <- tsenat(analysis)  # Access results via consistent S4 methods (type-safe, mutually-exclusive access instead of nested list indexing) diversity_results <- diversity(analysis) lm_table <- lmResults(analysis) jk_entropy <- jeoResults(analysis, q = 1.0) jk_iso <- jisResults(analysis, q = 1.0) rank_test <- rankResults(analysis) divergence_table <- divergence(analysis)

text: calculate transcript diversity measures (Shannon entropy, Simpson index, Tsallis entropy q=1 q=2), use: packages return SummarizedExperiment object, can investigate assay function.
code: # Create sample group classification based on sample names # (Normal samples end with _N, Tumor samples don't) sample_group <- ifelse(grepl("_N$", colnames(se_data)), "Normal", "Tumor")  # Add group metadata to se_data for all downstream analyses colData(se_data)$group <- sample_group  # SplicingFactory: Calculate diversity for both Shannon (naive) and Simpson methods sf_methods <- c("naive", "simpson") splicing_results <- setNames(vector("list", length(sf_methods)), sf_methods)  for (method in sf_methods) {   splicing_results[[method]] <- SplicingFactory::calculate_diversity(     x = se_data,     method = method,     norm = TRUE,     verbose = FALSE   )   # Add sample_type and group metadata to SplicingFactory objects   # (sample_type matches SplicingFactory naming; group matches TSENAT naming for consistency)   colData(splicing_results[[method]])$sample_type <- sample_group   colData(splicing_results[[method]])$group <- sample_group }  # TSENAT: Single config for q-value sweep # (Configuration is identical for all q-values) config <- tsenat_config(condition_col = "group")  # TSENAT: Create analysis objects and compute diversity for q=1 and q=2 q_values <- c(1, 2) tsenat_results <- setNames(vector("list", length(q_values)), paste0("q", q_values))  for (q in q_values) {   # Create analysis object (following Bioconductor pattern: config first, then constructor)   tsenat_results[[paste0("q", q)]] <- TSENATAnalysis(se_data, config = config)      # Compute diversity with dynamic output filename using sprintf   tsenat_results[[paste0("q", q)]] <- calculate_diversity_s4(     analysis = tsenat_results[[paste0("q", q)]],     q = q,     norm = TRUE,     verbose = FALSE   ) }  # Extract for downstream use (aliases maintain backward compatibility with existing code) shannon_entropy <- splicing_results$naive simpson_index <- splicing_results$simpson tsenat_analysis_q1 <- tsenat_results$q1 tsenat_analysis_q2 <- tsenat_results$q2

text: 1-gene difference SplicingFactory (214 genes tested) TSENAT (213 genes tested) due subtle important difference two packages filter genes statistical testing. Implementation Difference: SplicingFactory’s Implementation: problematic line uses sum(x$cond_1, x$cond_2), sums values column vectors together, producing single scalar (approximately 1,040 case). Since global sum always >= 8, condition essentially always TRUE, filtering ineffective. TSENAT’s Implementation: TSENAT uses (df$cond_1 + df$cond_2), performs element-wise addition check individual gene’s total observation count. consequence TSENAT’s filter stricter: requires gene individually least 8 total observations (3 one group, 3 , plus 2 either group). SplicingFactory’s filter effectively doesn’t work Wilcoxon test global sum condition almost never FALSE.
code: # SplicingFactory/R/calculate_difference.R (lines 163-164) x$cond_1 <- apply(x[grep(unique(samples)[1], samples) + 1], 1,                     function(x) sum(!is.na(x))) x$cond_2 <- apply(x[grep(unique(samples)[2], samples) + 1], 1,                     function(x) sum(!is.na(x)))  if (test == "wilcoxon") {     y <- x[x$cond_1 >= 3 & x$cond_2 >= 3 & sum(x$cond_1, x$cond_2) >= 8, ]     #                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^     #                                         This computes a SCALAR } # TSENAT/R/difference_helpers.R (lines 57-58) df$cond_1 <- rowSums(!is.na(df[, idx1 + 1, drop = FALSE])) df$cond_2 <- rowSums(!is.na(df[, idx2 + 1, drop = FALSE]))  if (test == "wilcoxon") {     keep_mask <- (df$cond_1 >= 3 & df$cond_2 >= 3 & (df$cond_1 + df$cond_2) >= 8)     #                                                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^     #                                                 Element-wise addition per gene }

title: TSENAT
text: Standard differential expression tools (DESeq2, edgeR) detect changes total transcript abundance. However, genes often reorganize isoform diversity without changing total abundance: may shift balanced isoform distribution dominance single isoform, vice versa. isoform switching splicing-driven regulation biologically important cell state function invisible abundance-focused methods.

title: TSENAT
text: TSENAT captures isoform complexity independently specific isoforms abundant. method uses Tsallis entropy sensitivity parameter q acts like lens: Low q (e.g., 0.5): Focuses rare isoforms - detects diversity maintained collapsed Mid q (e.g., 1.0): Balanced view (Shannon entropy) - overall isoform complexity High q (e.g., 2.0): Focuses dominant isoforms - detects dominance shifts examining diversity across multiple q-values, identify scale-dependent diversity changes - hallmark coordinate isoform switching.

title: TSENAT
text: Tsallis entropy parametric family diversity measures generalizes Shannon entropy enables tuning sensitivity different scales isoform organization. Mathematical Definition: discrete probability vector p=(p1,…,pn)p = (p_1, \ldots, p_n) representing isoform proportions within gene, Tsallis entropy : Sq=1−∑=1npiqq−1S_q = \frac{1 - \sum_{=1}^{n} p_i^q}{q - 1} elegant formula unifies diverse diversity concepts specific q-values: q = 0: Richness — Simple count expressed isoforms; emphasizes rare variants strongly. q = 1: Shannon entropy — Standard information-theoretic measure; balanced weighting across scales. q = 2: Gini-Simpson index — Probability two randomly-drawn transcripts different; robust rare variants. examining diversity across multiple q-values, identify scale-dependent diversity changes—hallmark coordinate isoform switching. See vignette(“TSENAT”) complete mathematical treatment information-theoretic interpretation.

what: Divergence Analysis: Measuring Information-Theoretic Distance Between Conditions
title: TSENAT
text: Tsallis entropy quantifies diversity within single distribution, Tsallis divergence DqD_q measures information-theoretic distance two distributions. Mathematical Definition: two probability distributions PP QQ representing isoform proportions control treatment conditions, Tsallis divergence : Dq(P||Q)=∑ipiq−∑ipi⋅qiq−1(q−1)∑ipiD_q(P||Q) = \frac{\sum_i p_i^q - \sum_i p_i \cdot q_i^{q-1}}{(q-1) \sum_i p_i} Tsallis divergence enables quantification fundamentally different isoform complexity patterns experimental conditions.

title: TSENAT
text: Generalized Additive Models (GAM) ARIMA Differencing: GAM semi-parametric approach using flexible smooth functions q group ARIMA(1,1,0) first-differencing remove monotone trend achieve stationarity. Estimates fixed effect parameters via smooth basis functions; automatically detects heteroscedasticity applies optimal variance weighting. Linear Mixed Models (LMM) AR(1): Fits mixed-effects models using nlme::lme() random intercept subject AR(1) correlation structure observation-level errors explicit time-ordering q-value. Generalized Estimating Equations (GEE) Multiple Correlation Structures: Fits marginal models three selectable correlation structures: AR(1) q-ordered data, exchangeable unordered measurements, independence. Includes Kauermann-Carroll bias correction small number clusters. Functional Principal Component Analysis (FPCA) Regularization: Treats entropy values ordered curves across q-values; applies ARIMA differencing performs PCA curve matrix extract orthogonal smooth principal components. Huber M-Estimation Leave-One-Diagnostics: Iteratively re-weighted least squares (IRLS) using Huber loss function.

title: TSENAT
text: Friedman Rank-Based Test Hochberg Correction: Non-parametric alternative repeated-measures ANOVA operates entirely ranks, requiring distributional assumptions. Jackknife via Delta Influence: Leave-one-resampling identify transcript-level contributors entropy changes via delta influence. Wilcoxon Rank Sum Test Multiple Hypothesis Correction: Unpaired paired (Wilcoxon signed-rank) non-parametric alternative t-tests. Permutation/Label Shuffling Test FDR Control: Non-parametric exact test via label shuffling.

title: TSENAT: Tsallis Entropy for Systems Evolutionary Analysis and Network Analysis Tool — TSENAT-package
text: Classical Shannon entropy (special case Tsallis q=1) treats probability states equally. Tsallis entropy order parameter \(q\) weights rare common transcripts differently: \(q < 1\): Emphasizes rare isoforms, capturing tail behavior \(q = 1\): Shannon entropy (equipartition weighting) \(q = 2\): Simpson entropy (dominance weighting, less sensitive rare species) \(q \\infty\): Reciprocal maximum transcript fraction multiscale perspective reveals condition-specific dependencies splicing architecture detects genes asymmetric isoform distributions traditional metrics miss.

title: TSENAT: Tsallis Entropy for Systems Evolutionary Analysis and Network Analysis Tool — TSENAT-package
text: TSENAT implements complete analytical pipeline: Diversity Quantification: Compute Tsallis entropy H_q across range     q-values (0 \(\infty\)) gene-condition group. Returns Hill numbers     (\(D_q = \exp(H_q)\)) interpretable effective isoform counts. Jackknife Resampling: Generate confidence intervals via leave-one-    resampling. Identifies genes statistically significant entropy outliers     condition-biased isoform usage (isoform switching). Linear Mixed Models: Tests gene--condition interaction effects     diversity landscapes using nlme, MASS, geepack backends. Supports paired designs     random effect structures. Divergence Analysis: Computes Tsallis divergence (generalized Kullback-Leibler)     condition groups. Detects differential transcript complexity via effect size     estimation. Visualization: Generates publication-ready plots: q-curves, volcano plots,     heatmaps, violin distributions, dimension-reduced embeddings.

title: TSENAT: Tsallis Entropy for Systems Evolutionary Analysis and Network Analysis Tool — TSENAT-package
text: Diversity Metrics Tsallis Entropy: \(H_q = \frac{1}{q-1} \left(1 - \sum_{} p_i^q\right)\)     Hill Numbers: \(D_q = \left(\sum_{} p_i^q\right)^{\frac{1}{1-q}}\) Divergence Tsallis Divergence: \(D_q(p||r) = \frac{1}{q-1}\left(1 - \sum_{} p_i^q r_i^{1-q}\right)\)     Kullback-Leibler distance (q=1 limit): \(D_{KL}(p||r) = \sum_i p_i \log(p_i/r_i)\) Resampling Jackknife leave-one-, block bootstrap (paired data), percentile/BCA confidence     intervals accuracy enhancement skewed distributions. Interaction Testing LMM: \(H_{g,c} = \beta_0 + \beta_g(\text{gene}) + \beta_c(\text{condition}) +     \beta_{gc}(\text{gene} \times \text{condition}) + \epsilon\)     random effects paired/nested designs.

title: TSENAT: Tsallis Entropy for Systems Evolutionary Analysis and Network Analysis Tool — TSENAT-package
text: q-value sweeps reveal biological complexity: Genes showing entropy     peaks intermediate q-values (0.5-1.5) suggest balanced isoform distributions;     peaks q \\infty indicate dominant-isoform architectures. Interaction q-profiles: q-dependent gene--condition interactions signal     condition-specific isoform switching; flat profiles indicate constitutive splicing. Divergence biological distance: Tsallis divergence quantifies     transcript composition distance; high divergence (D_q > 0.5) indicates distinct     splicing programs. Statistical interpretation: Jackknife CIs exclude point estimate     (valid skewed distributions) occur bounded entropies; software error.

title: Calculate divergence metrics and store in TSENATAnalysis — calculate_divergence_s4
text: Key Features: Multi-q analysis: Divergence computed across full q-spectrum simultaneously Bootstrap confidence intervals: Quantify uncertainty divergence estimates Multiple testing correction: Hochberg, Benjamini-Yekutieli, correction Paired designs: Supports paired/repeated measures via subject_col parameter Effect size reporting: Log-fold-change confidence intervals per gene Flexible control group: Compare condition vs. condition **Mathematical Background:** Tsallis divergence D_q two probability distributions: Measures much transcript composition changes control condition. Values near 0: Similar isoform composition; Large positive values: Major change. **Example Use Case:** Control sample: reads dominant isoform (low entropy) Tumor sample: Reads spread across multiple isoforms (high entropy) Result: Large divergence indicating condition-specific isoform switching. **Parameter Resolution:** Parameters resolved priority order: 1. Explicit arguments passed function 2. Values analysis@config (present) 3. Function defaults Requires diversity results calculate_diversity_s4() prerequisite.
code: D_q(P||Q) = (log_2(N) - entropy_q(P) + entropy_q(Q)) / (q - 1)

title: Calculate diversity and store in TSENATAnalysis — calculate_diversity_s4
text: Key Features: Multi-q analysis: Entropy computed q = 0.01 2.00 (default) Normalized entropy: Scale [0, 1] using theoretical maximum log(m) Bootstrap confidence intervals: Quantify uncertainty estimates TPM normalization: Optional SALMON TPM-based weighting Multiple normalization methods: Range, Z-score, log-odds-ratio, relative Spectrum computation: Aggregate diversity statistics across q-values **Mathematical Background:** Tsallis entropy H_q q-parameter: p_i = relative abundance isoform gene. Larger q emphasizes dominant isoforms; smaller q emphasizes rare ones. **Example Interpretation:** Gene 1 isoform: H_q = 0 q (diversity) Gene 2 equal isoforms: H_q ~ 0.5-1.0 depending q Gene m equally abundant isoforms: H_q = 1.0 (maximum diversity) wrapper calls .calculate_diversity() per q-value, storing results SummarizedExperiment objects. extracts key parameters analysis@config priority resolution (explicit > @config > default). **Diversity Spectrum Computation:** default, function computes saves diversity spectrum (aggregated statistics across q-values  groups) output_file provided. spectrum contains: q: Diversity parameter value central: Median (mean) diversity across genes spread: IQR (SD) around central value count: Number valid measurements group: Condition group (applicable) provides quick summary diversity changes across q-values, useful q-curve visualization statistical comparisons. Spectrum saved : *_spectrum.tsv **Parameter Priority Resolution:** q Priority 1 (explicit) > Priority 2 (@config$q_values) > Priority 3 (default:  seq(0. 01,  2,  = 0. 05))     **Note: ** explicit q @config$q_values provided,  explicit wins. nthreads Priority: explicit > @config$nthreads > 1 verbose Priority: explicit > @config$verbose > TRUE bootstrap Priority: explicit > @config$bootstrap > FALSE pseudocount Priority: explicit > @config$pseudocount > 0 norm Priority: explicit > @config$norm > TRUE Priority:  explicit > @config$> 'S' (Tsallis entropy) **Audit Trail:** execution, check: analysis@config$last_diversity_run$parameters_used:  Actual parameters         (original @config) attr(diversity(analysis,  q=X),  'computed_with'):  Per-q-value metadata         (timestamp, bootstrap setting, nthreads, etc.) additional details diversity spectrum calculations normalization methods, see package vignettes.
code: H_q(X) = (1/(q-1)) * (1 - Sum p_i^q)  [for q != 1]   H_1(X) = -Sum p_i * log(p_i)  [Shannon entropy, limit q→1]

code: # Create test analysis with appropriate sample structure for paired design # Note: requires lme4 package for LMM fitting; uses synthetic data set.seed(42)  # Create transcript-level counts with biological signal # Note: Use adequate complexity (transcripts/genes, samples, expression)  # to avoid filtering away all genes during diversity computation n_genes <- 50 n_transcripts_per_gene <- 30 n_transcripts <- n_genes * n_transcripts_per_gene n_samples <- 16  # 8 subjects x 2 conditions (paired design)  # Generate counts with clear biological signal control_idx <- seq(1, n_samples, by = 2) treatment_idx <- seq(2, n_samples, by = 2)  counts <- matrix(0, nrow = n_transcripts, ncol = n_samples) for (j in seq_len(n_samples)) {   lambda <- if (j %in% control_idx) 100 else 180   counts[, j] <- rpois(n_transcripts, lambda = lambda) } counts <- pmax(counts, 50)  # Ensure minimum expression  rownames(counts) <- paste0('TX_', seq_len(n_transcripts)) colnames(counts) <- paste0('Sample_', seq_len(n_samples))  # Create rowData with gene mapping (tx2gene structure) rowdata <- data.frame(   transcript_id = rownames(counts),   gene_id = rep(paste0('GENE_', 1:n_genes),                  each = n_transcripts_per_gene),   row.names = rownames(counts) )  # Create colData with paired design metadata coldata <- data.frame(   sample_id = colnames(counts),   condition = rep(c('control', 'treatment'),                    length.out = n_samples),   subject = rep(paste0('Subject_', 1:8),                  length.out = n_samples),   row.names = colnames(counts) )  # Build SummarizedExperiment se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(   assays = list(counts = counts),   rowData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(rowdata),   colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(coldata) )  # Add tx2gene metadata for gene-level aggregation S4Vectors::metadata(se)$tx2gene <-    data.frame(Transcript = rowdata$transcript_id,              Gene = rowdata$gene_id)  # Initialize TSENATAnalysis analysis <- TSENATAnalysis(se = se, config = list())  # Compute diversity (prerequisite for LM interaction analysis) analysis <- calculate_diversity_s4(   analysis,    q = c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5) )  # Calculate q x condition interactions using GAM analysis <- calculate_lm_interaction_s4(   analysis,   condition_col = 'condition',   method = 'gam' )  # View top interaction results (first 3 genes) res <- lmResults(analysis, 'lm_interaction') if (!is.null(res)) head(res, 3) #>      gene p_interaction        p_raw n_observations n_subjects n_effective #> 1  GENE_2  3.243028e-11 3.243028e-11             64         16    14.91552 #> 2 GENE_16  2.846394e-10 2.846394e-10             64         16    12.63764 #> 3 GENE_12  3.813131e-10 3.813131e-10             64         16    12.21766 #>      rho_ar1 test_statistic effect_size df_residual model_converged #> 1 0.04696714       48.30386   0.8654711    58.00221            TRUE #> 2 0.15914471       43.95960   0.8297352    58.00643            TRUE #> 3 0.18223084       43.37480   0.8236480    58.00825            TRUE #>      slope_diff arima_transformation bounded_support_model family_used #> 1  1.883577e-06                 TRUE                 FALSE    Gaussian #> 2 -3.589224e-06                 TRUE                 FALSE    Gaussian #> 3 -1.424366e-05                 TRUE                 FALSE    Gaussian #>   heteroscedasticity_detected variance_ratio_q              fit_method #> 1                       FALSE         2.361163 mgcv::gamm_arima(1,1,0) #> 2                       FALSE         3.511304 mgcv::gamm_arima(1,1,0) #> 3                        TRUE         3.882614 mgcv::gamm_arima(1,1,0) #>   shapiro_p_value residuals_normal n_residuals_tested ci_weighted #> 1     0.076530821             TRUE                 64       FALSE #> 2     0.003200931            FALSE                 64       FALSE #> 3     0.264509774             TRUE                 64       FALSE #>   adj_p_interaction gene_name gene_id #> 1      1.621514e-09    GENE_2  GENE_2 #> 2      1.394733e-08   GENE_16 GENE_16 #> 3      1.830303e-08   GENE_12 GENE_12

text: wrapper applies .filter_se() SummarizedExperiment within TSENATAnalysis object, optionally followed subsetting parameters. filtering subsetting operations applied sequence: 1. title: Jackknife isoform switching analysis on TSENATAnalysis object — jackknife_isoform_switching_s4
text: Key Features: Jackknife resampling: Robust outlier detection across samples Delta-influence metric: Measures much isoform drives phenotype Confidence intervals: Bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification Multi-q analysis: Tests across full q-spectrum simultaneously LM filtering: Optional restriction genes significant interactions Paired designs: Supports repeated measures/longitudinal data **Parameter Resolution Config** following parameters resolved using three-level priority system: User-provided argument (NULL) Value analysis@config (key exists) Function default value Affected parameters: q: Uses config's q_values available, else c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2) n_bootstrap: Uses config's n_bootstrap available, else 1000 threshold: Uses config's threshold available, else 90 lm_p_threshold: Uses config's lm_p_threshold available, else 0.05 allows setting defaults config reusing across multiple analyses. **Mathematical Background:** Delta-influence measures much removing sample changes entropy: High |Delta| specific isoforms indicates isoforms drive differences. Identifies 'outlier samples' isoforms contribute unusually much. **Example Use Case:** Sample shows high Delta isoform X → X outsized importance sample Classifying transcripts 'switching' top percentile (e.g., 90th) Delta Reveals condition-specific isoforms crucial phenotype determination. **Automatic Setup:** wrapper automatically: 1. Extracts SummarizedExperiment @se slot 2. Detects condition_col, gene_col, isoform_col colData/rowData @config 3. Calls .jackknife_isoform_switching() extracted parameters **Parameter Auto-Detection:** condition_col:  Uses explicit parameter,  @config,  'sample_type' gene_col:  Uses explicit parameter,  looks 'gene'  'Gene' isoform_col:  Uses explicit parameter,  looks 'transcript',  'isoform',   'Isoform'

title: M-Estimation for Sample Quality (S4 Wrapper) — m_estimate_s4
text: Modified TSENATAnalysis object M-estimation results stored analysis@metadata$m_estimate_results. Contains data frame influence scores, robustness weights, entropy statistics, QC classifications. Returns visibly support method chaining piping.

title: M-Estimation for Sample Quality (S4 Wrapper) — m_estimate_s4
text: wrapper extracts diversity results analysis@diversity_results, performs robust M-estimation diversity values (entropy), stores results analysis object metadata. **M-Estimation:** Robust regression technique -weights outliers based residuals. Useful detecting low-quality samples show unusual diversity patterns. **M-Estimation Results include:** sample_influence: much sample affects overall fit robustness_weight:  -weighting factor (lower = outlying) entropy_mean: Average entropy sample entropy_sd: Entropy variability within sample Status:  QC Classification ('OK'  'Flag QC' based influence_threshold) **Parameter resolution priority** (explicit > @config > error): samples: Uses explicit arg, else @config$condition_col, else error. Note: despite parameter name 'samples', maps condition grouping column **Data Requirements:** Diversity results must computed via calculate_diversity_s4() Sample grouping column required colData (auto-detected @config$condition_col     via 'samples' parameter)

title: M-Estimation for Sample Quality (S4 Wrapper) — m_estimate_s4
code: # Create test analysis and compute M-estimation data(readcounts) readcounts <- as.matrix(readcounts) mode(readcounts) <- 'numeric' metadata_df <- read.table(   system.file('extdata', 'metadata.tsv', package = 'TSENAT'),   header = TRUE, sep = '\t' ) gff3_dataset <- system.file('extdata', 'annotation.gff3.gz', package = 'TSENAT')  # Create config (metadata passed as explicit parameter to build_analysis_s4) config <- tsenat_config(   sample_col = 'sample',   condition_col = 'condition',   q_values = seq(0, 2, by = 0.05),   paired = FALSE )  # Build analysis from vignette data analysis <- build_analysis_s4(   readcounts = readcounts,   tx2gene = gff3_dataset,   metadata = metadata_df,   config = config,   tpm = tpm,   effective_length = effective_length ) analysis <- filter_analysis_s4(analysis, min_samples = 1, subset_n_genes = 200) analysis <- calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, q = c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5)) #> Note: 12 genes excluded (< 75% valid values). analysis <- m_estimate_s4(   analysis,   condition_col = 'condition',   loss_type = 'huber' )

text: Key Features: Multi-gene grid: Side--side comparison top N genes (default: 9) q-spectrum curves: Per-gene divergence across q = 0.01 2.00 Bootstrap CI bands: 95 Statistical significance: Gene titles include adjusted p-values Automatic layout: Grid dimensions auto-calculated n_genes q=1 reference line: KL divergence (information theory benchmark) Region labels: Rare (q<1) vs Abundant (q>1) isoform emphasis Creates multi-panel grid comparing per-q divergence profiles across top N genes identified LMM interaction analysis. panel shows full q-spectrum divergence curve gene name adjusted p-value title. **Mathematical Background:** Tsallis divergence function q: q < 1: Emphasizes rare isoforms (sensitive outliers) q = 1: Kullback-Leibler divergence (classical information theory) q > 1: Emphasizes abundant isoforms (robust rare variants) D_q varies across q-spectrum, showing complexity isoform differences. **Example Interpretation:** Flat curve: Divergence stable across q (robust isoform difference) Curved pattern: q-dependent divergence (rare vs abundant isoforms differ) Peaks high q: Main isoforms drive difference, rare ones immaterial **Input Modes:** - **Mode 1 (Primary)**: Pass eff_res directly (effect_sizes_divergence) - **Mode 2 (Fallback)**: Pass lm_res + divergence_results_se instead **Gene Filtering:** Genes ranked decreasing statistical significance (increasing adj_p_interaction). genes complete per-q divergence data included. fewer n_genes valid data, function returns available genes. **Plot Features:** - Title shows: gene name adjusted p-value (q-value format) - Per-q divergence curve point estimates 95 - Vertical reference line q=1 (Kullback-Leibler divergence point) - Region labels: 'Rare Isoforms' (q<1), 'Balanced' (q~=1), 'Abundant Isoforms' (q>1) - plots use consistent ggplot2 styling matching plot_q_spectrum

Increased for statistical power n_samples <- n_samples_per_group * 2  # Generate control and treatment with very strong separation # This ensures sufficient statistical power for divergence tests control_counts <- matrix(rpois(n_isoforms * n_samples_per_group, lambda = 100),   nrow = n_isoforms, ncol = n_samples_per_group) treatment_counts <- matrix(rpois(n_isoforms * n_samples_per_group, lambda = 300),   nrow = n_isoforms, ncol = n_samples_per_group) counts <- cbind(control_counts, treatment_counts) rownames(counts) <- paste0('TX_', 1:n_isoforms) colnames(counts) <- paste0('Sample_', 1:n_samples)  se <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(counts = counts)) tx2gene_df <- data.frame(Transcript = rownames(counts),   Gene = rep(paste0('GENE_', 1:n_genes), each = n_isoforms_per_gene)) S4Vectors::metadata(se)$tx2gene <- tx2gene_df SummarizedExperiment::colData(se) <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(   sample_id = paste0('Sample_', 1:n_samples),   condition = rep(c('control', 'treatment'), each = n_samples_per_group),   row.names = colnames(se)) SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)$transcript_id <- rownames(se) SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)$gene_id <- tx2gene_df$Gene[match(rownames(se),   tx2gene_df$Transcript)]  # Run complete analysis pipeline (skipped for speed in documentation) # Uncomment to run actual analysis: # analysis <- TSENATAnalysis(se) # analysis <- calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, q = c(0.5, 1, 1.5),  #   nboot = 50) # analysis <- calculate_divergence_s4(analysis, q = c(0.5, 1, 1.5),  #   nboot = 50) # analysis <- calculate_lm_interaction_s4(analysis, #   condition_col = 'condition') # analysis <- effect_sizes_divergence_s4(analysis) # p <- plot_multi_gene_q_spectrum_s4(analysis, n_genes = 4) # if (!is.null(p)) print(p)

code: # Load example data (matching TSENAT.Rmd workflow) data(readcounts) readcounts <- as.matrix(readcounts) mode(readcounts) <- 'numeric' metadata_df <- read.table(   system.file('extdata', 'metadata.tsv', package = 'TSENAT'),   header = TRUE, sep = '\t' ) gff3_dataset <- system.file('extdata', 'annotation.gff3.gz', package = 'TSENAT')  # Build analysis from vignette data and create small subset config <- tsenat_config(   sample_col = 'sample',   condition_col = 'condition',   q_values = seq(0, 2, by = 0.05),   paired = FALSE ) analysis <- build_analysis_s4(   readcounts = readcounts,   metadata = metadata_df,   tx2gene = gff3_dataset,   config = config,   tpm = tpm,   effective_length = effective_length ) analysis <- filter_analysis_s4(analysis, min_samples = 1, subset_n_genes = 200) analysis <- calculate_diversity_s4(analysis, q = c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5)) #> Note: 12 genes excluded (< 75% valid values). analysis <- test_rankbased_assumptions_s4(analysis, q = 1.0) # Access results using getMeta S4 accessor names(getMeta(analysis, 'rankbased_assumptions')) #> [1] "result"           "q_value_tested"   "checks_performed" "alpha_used"       #> [5] "timestamp"

title: Create and return TSENAT configuration — tsenat_config
text: q_values numeric. Q-values Tsallis entropy spectrum. Default: seq(0, 2, = 0.5). condition_col character. Name column colData(se) containing experimental conditions/groups. Default: 'condition'. subject_col character. Name column colData(se) containing subject/sample identifiers paired/repeated designs. provided, enables paired analysis. Default: NULL (unpaired). sample_col character. Name column colData(se) containing sample identifiers. Default: 'sample'. paired logical. Whether samples paired/repeated measures. Default: FALSE. Used jackknife difference analysis. control character. Reference/control group label difference analysis (e.g., 'control', 'wt'). used 'difference' methods. Default: NULL. p_threshold numeric. Raw p-value threshold significance LM interaction testing. Default: 0.05. fdr_threshold numeric. Adjusted p-value (FDR/Benjamini-Hochberg) threshold. Default: 0.05. significance_threshold numeric. Significance cutoff effect sizes, assumptions testing, result filtering. Default: 0.05. nboot integer. Number bootstrap resamples jackknife confidence intervals. Default: 1000. bootstrap_method character. Bootstrap CI method: 'percentile' (fast, assumes symmetric distribution) 'bca' (bias-corrected, better skewed data like bounded entropy). Default: 'percentile'. stringency character. Transcript filtering stringency level. Options: 'lenient' (minimal filtering), 'medium' (default, reasonable filtering), 'severe' (strict filtering, recommended high-confidence results). Controls transcripts/genes retained initial filtering step. Default: 'medium'. nthreads integer. Number threads parallel computation supported (diversity, divergence, LM fitting). Default: 1 (parallelization). Use 2+ multi-core systems improve performance. ... Additional configuration parameters (stored -@config slot). Examples: q_diff=1.0 (specific q differences), alpha=0.05 (significance assumptions), etc.

title: TSENAT 0.99.0
text: Initial Bioconductor release. TSENAT provides scale-dependent analysis transcript isoform diversity using Tsallis entropy, enabling detection splicing-driven regulatory changes orthogonal count-based differential expression methods. Core analysis via calculate_diversity() / calculate_diversity_s4(), calculate_difference() / calculate_difference_s4(), calculate_divergence() / calculate_divergence_s4(), calculate_lm_interaction() / calculate_lm_interaction_s4() supporting diverse statistical tests (Wilcoxon, Friedman, permutation, jackknife bootstrap). Parameter q tunes Tsallis entropy sensitivity: q < 1 emphasizes rare isoforms, q ≈ 1 recovers Shannon entropy, q > 1 emphasizes dominant isoforms. Unified S4 class TSENATAnalysis integrating SummarizedExperiment, configuration, results, cached plots full subsetting accessor support. Data input: read_salmon_samples() direct Salmon/Sailfish quantification import GFF3 annotation parsing. Quality control: filter_analysis_s4() multi-criteria filtering; jackknife_entropy_outliers_s4() outlier detection. Visualization suite (8 plot types): diversity q-curves, volcano/MA plots, violin/density plots, transcript composition heatmaps, divergence distance matrices, interaction surfaces, concordance plots, multi-gene q-spectrum plots. ggplot2-based publication-ready styling. High-level workflow orchestration via tsenat() flexible configuration management tsenat_config(). Performance: Rcpp/RcppArmadillo entropy calculations, BiocParallel support, lazy-loading visualization libraries (~30% faster non-plot workflows). Comprehensive documentation: main vignette + 2 appendices (SplicingFactory validation, advanced workflows), 46 exported functions complete roxygen2 documentation.
